title: A torsion-free module over a principal ideal domain is flat
statement: Let $A$ be a principal ideal domain (an integral domain in which every ideal is generated by one element) and $M$ an $A$-module which is torsion free: if $a\in A$, $a\neq0$, $m\in M$ and $am=0$, then $m=0$. Then $M$ is a flat $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AUW (lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat, line 4954), part (1), for a PID (which is a Dedekind domain, Algebra Lemma PID-dedekind, cited in its proof); valuation ring case Lemma Tag 0539 (lemma-valuation-ring-torsion-free-flat)

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: `Module.Flat.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot_of_isBezout [IsBezout R] [IsDomain R] : Module.Flat R M ↔ Submodule.torsion R M = ⊥` (TorsionFree.lean:93); a PID is `IsDomain` and `IsPrincipalIdealRing`, hence `IsBezout` by the instance IsBezout.of_isPrincipalIdealRing (Mathlib/RingTheory/PrincipalIdealDomain.lean:69); `Submodule.torsion R M` (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Torsion/Basic.lean:201) is the set of m killed by a non-zero-divisor, and in a domain the non-zero-divisors are the nonzero elements (mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_ne_zero), so `torsion R M = ⊥` is the torsion-free hypothesis.
